second_order: making and playing along with the room's April Fools jokes
theme_note: These passages all make, explain, solicit attention to, or react to the room's own jokes rather than the canvas; they vary from a bare meme and altered titles to a death-hoax announcement and brief audience reactions.

second_order: rallying help to build and defend the Fox Stevenson logo
theme_note: These codes recruit and acknowledge people for the shared work of getting a Fox Stevenson mark onto the canvas; they vary between proposing it, volunteering, asking for coordination, starting work, calling for multiple accounts or all hands, and announcing active building.

second_order: simplifying and sharing how the logo should look
theme_note: These passages make the proposed mark buildable by reducing it to a stem or circulating text placement and pixel art; what varies is whether the contributor simplifies, lays out text, or supplies the picture.

second_order: relocating when other builds take the space
theme_note: These codes track the practical work of abandoning occupied coordinates and trying another place; they vary from responding to Samurai Jack's rebuild, to a third location, to discovering another link and finally naming insufficient space and manpower.

second_order: making room for Aku and trading help
theme_note: These turns negotiate a collision with r/samuraijack by explaining the Aku rebuild, asking that it be left room, and offering later help; the shared practice is working out who builds there, while the turns vary between account, request, and reciprocal offer.

second_order: teaming up with Liquicity and sending helpers to Discord
theme_note: These turns establish contact, propose building two neighbouring logos together, direct would-be helpers to Liquicity's Discord, and acknowledge that direction; they vary between alliance-making and moving part of the help off-platform.

second_order: settling for half a logo when time ran out
theme_note: This single code records the participant's own retrospective compromise after the build did not finish; it does not share the recruiting, designing, relocating, negotiating, or venue-moving practice of the other groups.
